Extreme heat killed nearly 3 million people worldwide in eight years
Between 2016 and 2023, around three million people died as a result of extreme heat.
It was noted in a report published in the British scientific journal The Lancet and prepared by more than 140 researchers.
The climate report proposes declaring a global public health emergency over climate change to push governments to adjust their climate policies.
Researchers say most of the deaths were directly linked to the climate crisis.
According to the report, heat-related deaths reached a record 710,000 in 2023, with more than 70% attributed to human-caused climate change. Marina Romanello, executive director of the Lancet Countdown project, said nearly three million people worldwide had died from heat in the eight years since the Paris Agreement was signed in 2015.
Speaking at a press conference, she said the figure was equivalent to the entire population of Wales dying from heat over roughly eight years.
Romanello added that 68% of the deaths were directly linked to the climate crisis.

MUQDISHO — Guddoomiyaha Golaha Shacabka ee Baarlamaanka Federaalka Soomaaliya, Cabdulqaadir Maxamed Nuur (Jaamac), ayaa kulan la qaatay madaxda warbaahinta gaarka loo leeyahay, kaas oo looga hadlay xoojinta wada shaqeynta Golaha Shacabka iyo warbaahinta, ilaalinta madaxbannaanida saxaafadda iyo dhowrista xorriyadda hadalka.
Kulanka ayaa diiradda lagu saaray xoojinta xiriirka u dhexeeya Golaha Shacabka iyo warbaahinta, daahfurnaanta, gudbinta xog sugan, ka hortagga wararka been-abuurka ah iyo kor u qaadista wacyiga bulshada Soomaaliyeed.
Guddoomiye Cabdulqaadir Maxamed Nuur ayaa sheegay inuu aaminsan yahay in warbaahinta xorta ah, oo qabata dabagal iyo dhaliil wax dhisaysa, ay door muhiim ah ka qaadato horumarka dalka, daahfurnaanta iyo isla xisaabtanka hay’adaha dowladda.
Wuxuu carrabka ku adkeeyay in warbaahintu ay tahay tiir muhiim u ah isku xirka Golaha Shacabka iyo bulshada Soomaaliyeed, isaga oo xusay muhiimadda ay leedahay wada shaqeyn ku dhisan isfaham, furfurnaan iyo dhowrista xorriyadda saxaafadda.
Guddoomiyaha ayaa sidoo kale madaxda warbaahinta ugu baaqay inay kaalin ka qaataan ka hortagga faafinta wararka been-abuurka ah iyo dacaayadaha, kuwaas oo uu sheegay inay u adeegaan Al-Shabaab iyo kooxo ama shaqsiyaad kale oo doonaya inay waxyeelleeyaan danaha qaranka iyo dowladnimada Soomaaliyeed.
Wuxuu ku boorriyay warbaahinta inay xoojiso wacyigelinta bulshada, isla markaana ay ku dadaasho tebinta warar sugan oo masuuliyad ku dhisan, kana tarjumaya danta guud.
Kulankan ayaa imanaya xilli ay sii kordhayaan doodo la xiriira kaalinta saxaafadda madaxbannaan ay ku leedahay isla xisaabtanka, daahfurnaanta iyo xiriirka u dhexeeya hay’adaha dowladda iyo shacabka.
Warbaahinta Soomaaliya waxaa ku jira telefishinno, idaacado, wargeysyo iyo mareegaha wararka ee dowladda iyo kuwa gaarka loo leeyahay. Suxufiyiinta dalka ayaa weli wajahaya caqabado la xiriira amniga, xiisadaha siyaasadeed iyo ilaalinta xorriyadda saxaafadda.
Ujeeddooyinka kulanka waxaa ka mid ahaa xoojinta wada shaqeynta Golaha Shacabka iyo warbaahinta gaarka loo leeyahay, iyadoo la dhiirrigelinayo tebinta xog sugan iyo saxaafad masuuliyad ku dhisan.

DOOXA, Qatar — Soomaaliya ayaa fursadaha maalgashi ee dalka ku soo bandhigtay Madasha 9-aad ee Maalgashiga Adduunka (WIF 2026), oo ka dhacday magaalada Dooxa ee dalka Qatar, iyadoo Wasiiru Dowlaha Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibadda iyo Iskaashiga Caalamiga ah, Cali Maxamed Cumar (Cali Balcad), uu ku baaqay in la xoojiyo iskaashiga lala leeyahay maalgashadayaasha caalamiga ah iyo ganacsiga gaarka loo leeyahay.
Cali Balcad ayaa ka qayb galay dood heer sare ah oo diiradda lagu saaray doorka maalgashiga ganacsiga gaarka loo leeyahay ee maalgelinta horumarinta dalalka soo koraya.
Intii ay dooddu socotay, wasiiru dowluhu wuxuu Soomaaliya ku tilmaamay dal leh fursado maalgashi oo sii kobcaya, isaga oo xusay dhammaystirka hannaanka cafinta deymaha dalka iyo hirgelinta Sharciga cusub ee Maalgashiga, kuwaas oo uu ku tilmaamay tallaabooyin muhiim u ah hagaajinta jawiga maalgashiga.
Wuxuu carrabka ku adkeeyay muhiimadda ay leedahay in la xoojiyo iskaashiga lala leeyahay maalgashadayaasha iyo ganacsatada gaarka loo leeyahay, si loo helo maalgelin wax ku ool ah oo taageerta horumarka qaranka iyo kobaca dhaqaalaha Soomaaliya.
Soomaaliya ayaa dadaal ugu jirta dib-u-dhiska dhaqaalaha dalka iyo soo jiidashada maalgashiga shisheeye, kaddib sannado ay jireen colaado iyo caqabado dhaqaale. Cafinta deymaha ayaa ahayd tallaabo muhiim ah oo gacan ka geysatay dib u soo celinta kalsoonida dhaqaale ee dalka iyo ballaarinta fursadaha uu ku heli karo maalgelinta horumarineed ee caalamiga ah.
Dowladda ayaa sidoo kale ku howlan hagaajinta nidaamka sharciyeed ee ganacsiga iyo dhiirrigelinta doorka ganacsiga gaarka loo leeyahay ee qaybaha kala duwan ee dhaqaalaha.
Ka qaybgalka Cali Balcad ee madasha ayaa fursad u siisay Soomaaliya inay soo bandhigto mudnaanta dhaqaale ee dalka, isla markaana ay la yeelato daneeyayaasha caalamiga ah wadahadallo ku saabsan iskaashiyo maalgashi oo suurtagal ah.
Madasha Maalgashiga Adduunka ayaa isu keenta mas’uuliyiin dowladeed, maalgashadayaal, hoggaamiyeyaasha ganacsiga iyo hay’adaha horumarinta, si ay uga wada hadlaan xeeladaha maalgashiga iyo helitaanka maalgelin lagu dardargelinayo horumarka waara.
Farriinta Soomaaliya ee madasha ayaa xoogga saartay muhiimadda ay leedahay wada shaqeyn dhow oo dhex marta dowladda, maalgashadayaasha gaarka loo leeyahay iyo saaxiibbada caalamiga ah, si looga faa’iideysto fursadaha maalgashi loona taageero kobac dhaqaale oo waara.
War-saxaafadeedka laguma shaacin heshiisyo maalgashi oo gaar ah ama ballanqaadyo dhaqaale oo ka dhashay doodda.

Nigerian climate activists have spent the last week warning Nigerians about the potential impact of the El Niño heatwave on the country.
Although it has become a trending topic, some Nigerians still know nothing about the heatwave, and in this article, we cover everything you need to know about El Niño.
What is El Niño?
El Niño is a natural climate pattern that occurs where surface waters in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean become warmer than the average temperature. This warming alters global atmospheric circulation and can disrupt normal weather patterns worldwide.
It is a phenomenon that typically occurs every two-seven years and can last between nine and twelve months in the year.
Why Is El Niño Suddenly a Trending Topic?
The reason El Niño is a trending topic in Nigeria is due to the World Meteorological Organization confirming a strong El Niño wave for 2026. The heatwave is reported to peak by late 2026 and carry on into 2027.
It is reportedly expected to be the strongest El Niño ever measured for this time of year, and the WMO has said it will likely be the strongest on record, already classified as a “very strong El Niño,” also known as a super El Niño.
The World Meteorological Organization is expecting it to peak by November or December and last through the early months of 2027.
How It is Impacting Nigeria
El Niño is expected to affect Nigeria’s weather by causing regional variations in unusual heat, rainfall and shifting climate patterns.
The Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet) and the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) have reported or warned of unusually high temperatures and heat-related health issues due to the strong pattern of the El Niño wave.
Tips to Stay Safe During El Niño
The most important tip to staying safe during the El Niño event is following official guidance from the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) and weather agencies like NiMet. El Niño can bring extreme heat, heavy rainfall, or flooding, depending on the region affected.
However, some easy tips to help you stay safe are:
- Staying Hydrated
Heat can be draining; to stay ahead of it, drink clean water regularly throughout the day, even if you don’t feel thirsty.
- Limit your time in the sun
It is important to stay out of direct sunlight as much as possible. Avoid peak sunlight and strenuous activities between 11am and 4pm.
- Dress for the weather
In extreme heatwaves, wear light, loose clothing, hats, and sunglasses to help you stay out of the sun and reduce the risk of heat-related illness.
- Learn heatstroke signs
Watch for heavy sweating, dizziness, headache, or confusion. If someone shows signs of heatstroke, move them to a cool place, apply wet clothes, and seek emergency help immediately.
In cases of El Niño bringing flooding, these are the tips to stay safe:
- Clean your drainage
Keep your home gutters, drains, and nearby waterways clean and free of refuse that could reduce proper water flow in flooded areas.
- Protect your drinking water
A major concern is water contamination, so store clean water early in covered, waterproof containers before shortages or contamination occur.
- Avoid floodwaters
Never walk, swim, or drive through moving or stagnant floodwaters to protect from diseases or drowning.
What do we think?
The most important thing to know about the El Niño event is that you should follow tips from weather and health experts who share tips and updates on how to protect yourself and remain safe.

Hyderabad: Rainfall activity is likely to ease across
Telangana on Thursday, with light to moderate showers expected at isolated places. However, the
India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a yellow alert for thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds of 30–40 kmph in 12 districts.
The warning covers Komuram Bheem Asifabad, Mancherial, Rajanna Sircilla, Karimnagar, Peddapalli, Jayashankar Bhupalpally, Mulugu, Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam, Mahabubabad, Warangal and Hanumakonda.
In Hyderabad, the forecast for Thursday is partly cloudy skies and hazy conditions during the morning hours. The maximum temperature is expected to hover around 32°C, while the minimum is likely to be 22°C. Isolated rainfall is also possible.
On Wednesday, the impact of Cyclone Arnab was felt across several parts of Telangana. Rainfall ranging from 10 mm to 21.3 mm was recorded in parts of Khammam, Mulugu, Suryapet and Bhadradri Kothagudem by early afternoon, according to the Telangana Development Planning Society.
Nalgonda, Mahabubabad, Warangal and Jayashankar Bhupalpally received rainfall of up to 10 mm. The IMD had issued an orange alert for heavy to very heavy rainfall in Khammam, Bhadradri Kothagudem, Nalgonda and Suryapet.
Hyderabad recorded a maximum temperature of 27.2°C on Wednesday, marking a drop of 5°C compared with the previous day’s maximum.
The very severe cyclonic storm crossed the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts on Wednesday morning, bringing heavy rainfall and strong winds to parts of the region before weakening as it moved inland.

full_text:
Bhubaneswar: Cyclone Arnab battered coastal Andhra Pradesh with winds reaching 150 kmph on Wednesday, leaving at least three people dead, uprooting trees and disrupting power supplies, while torrential rain lashed neighbouring Odisha, forcing the evacuation of more than 30,000 people.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said the very severe cyclonic storm crossed the Andhra Pradesh–Yanam coast between 2 am and 8 am, packing sustained winds of 125–135 kmph and gusts reaching 150 kmph. The system subsequently weakened into a severe cyclonic storm but continued to threaten southern Odisha with heavy to extremely heavy rainfall.
The IMD issued a red warning for six Odisha districts — Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri and Nabarangpur — forecasting isolated extremely heavy rainfall and winds of 60–70 kmph, gusting up to 85 kmph in some areas.
Gajapati and Ganjam bore the brunt of the downpour, with Mahendragarh in Gajapati recording 249.9 mm of rainfall. Intermittent rain also lashed Bhubaneswar, Cuttack, Puri, Dhenkanal and Berhampur.
The heavy rainfall triggered waterlogging and raised fears of flooding in low-lying areas, overflowing streams and landslides in hilly regions. Strong winds also threatened to uproot trees, damage houses and disrupt electricity supplies.
The Odisha government evacuated more than 30,000 people from vulnerable areas, including low-lying villages and landslide-prone locations. Disaster-response teams were deployed, while district administrations were directed to remain prepared for emergencies.
Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi reviewed relief and restoration operations at Lok Seva Bhawan. Deputy Chief Minister Kanak Vardhan Singh Deo visited Koraput district and distributed relief materials among affected residents.
Meanwhile, Andhra Pradesh reported widespread damage, with uprooted trees, damaged houses and disrupted electricity supplies. At least three deaths were reported in initial assessments, while authorities began evaluating the extent of the destruction.
The IMD said the cyclone was likely to move north-northwestwards and weaken gradually. Fishermen were advised against venturing into the sea until October 29.
Authorities urged residents to avoid flooded roads and remain indoors during strong winds, warning that the threat of flooding and landslides could persist despite the cyclone weakening.
